context:
Goal: no lane leaves the shared checkout /home/user/claude-settings (the pointer checkout, the copy every session reads) off its recorded head.
Problem (rule): a lane's shell stood in that checkout and committed a merge on its detached head (from its old head to a new merge commit, on no branch, nothing pushed); the guard rule other-checkout (writes land only in your own checkout) refused the lane's `git switch -C main origin/main` from its worktree, so undoing it needs your override, a tool the lane's rules reserve for you, or no undo at all.
Based on (read): the lane's refusal text, relayed verbatim by the coordinator at 14:50 CST; the guard that stops a move of the shared checkout off main (rule pointer-head) never ran (not read by triage).
Based on (ruling): decision recovery-independent-of-state allows a move back to main with no override, but it does not cover a move made from inside a worktree, which other-checkout refuses first.
Departs from: main — no session can move the shared checkout's head from a worktree — options b and c let one move through; a changes nothing.
Waiting on: only the lane's pointer checkout; the lane's real work is in its worktree; the coordinator relays your answer to the lane. Unverified: whether this commit moves the guard's head for other sessions (the coordinator says its own guard reads a different copy of the rules than the shared checkout; triage did not measure this).

options.gain: No guard is let through and nothing more can go wrong.
options.how: No act. The stray merge commit stays on no branch in that checkout; the container ends with the session.
options.label: Leave it: the lane works in its own worktree and nothing is pushed (recommended)
options.lose: The shared checkout keeps a head that is not the recorded one until its container ends.

options.gain: The head is back on main with no override.
options.how: The lane leaves its worktree with ExitWorktree (action keep), runs the switch from the pointer checkout, and reports the result.
options.label: The lane calls ExitWorktree (keep), then runs `git switch -C main origin/main` in the shared checkout
options.lose: The lane uses a tool its own rules reserve for a user ask, and the guard that stops a move off main has never run on this case.

options.gain: The head is back on main by a path the guards name.
options.how: You type `override` (one act, not `override 15m`); the lane runs that one command.
options.label: Type `override` for one act so the lane's worktree session runs `git -C /home/user/claude-settings switch -C main origin/main`
options.lose: One guard (other-checkout) is let through, on a head move whose harm is unverified.

ref: coordinator message 14:50 CST Nov 18, relaying lane ci-cancel-on-close-v2 (verbatim result 14:49 CST)

Say so here if you want b or c instead.

title: A lane's merge moved the shared checkout's head to a commit on no branch: undo it, or leave it?
why: a costs nothing and the harm is unverified; b and c undo a head move that may not matter. Recommended by the coordinator, not owner-typed.
